chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The Mudabbir (slave manumitted upon death) is from the third (of the estate), and what he commits (of debts/damages) and the Mukatab (slave who pays for manumission in installments) and the Umm al-Walad (mother of the child) is borne by the master, so the master is liable for their liabilities.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: A slave woman who bears her master's child
key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرُ: A slave manumitted upon the master's death
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبُ: A slave who pays for manumission in installments

ai.seo_question: Who is financially liable for the debts of a Mudabbir, Mukatab, and Umm al-Walad in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the financial liability of the master for damages incurred by semi-free slaves, specifically categorizing the Mudabbir, Mukatab, and Umm al-Walad. It establishes that the master guarantees their debts, with the Mudabbir's estate share treated as one-third for settlement purposes, reflecting the juristic principle of shared responsibility in manumission stages. This ruling is crucial for understanding the economic rights and obligations within the Shia fiqh of manumission.
